Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping its gateway (192.168.10.1). Command prompt shows Destination host unreachable.
Show_Command_Output: PC1> ipconfig ... IP Address: 192.168.1.11, Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, Default Gateway: 192.168.10.1
Expected_Fault: PC1 has an incorrect IP address (192.168.1.11) that does not match the 192.168.10.0 subnet.

Symptom_Description: PC2 can ping local devices but fails to ping outside the subnet. Routing behaves incorrectly.
Show_Command_Output: PC2> ipconfig ... IP Address: 192.168.10.12, Subnet Mask: 255.255.0.0, Default Gateway: 192.168.10.1
Expected_Fault: PC2 has an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.0.0 instead of 255.255.255.0), causing routing confusion.

Symptom_Description: PC3 can ping local VLAN 20 devices, but cannot ping PC1 or the Router.
Show_Command_Output: PC3> ipconfig ... IP Address: 192.168.20.11, Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0, Default Gateway: 192.168.20.99
Expected_Fault: The default gateway IP on PC3 is typed incorrectly (192.168.20.99 instead of 192.168.20.1).

Symptom_Description: PC4 and PC3 have intermittent connectivity. Devices drop offline randomly.
Expected_Fault: Duplicate IP address. Both PC3 and PC4 are using 192.168.20.11.

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping its gateway. VLAN 10 is completely down.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip interface brief ... Gi0/0.10 192.168.100.1 up up
Expected_Fault: Router subinterface Gi0/0.10 has the wrong IP address (192.168.100.1) for the VLAN 10 subnet.

Symptom_Description: PC1 has no link light (red X on cable). Cannot ping anything.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show interfaces status ... Fa0/1 admin down down
Expected_Fault: Switch port FastEthernet0/1 is administratively shut down.

Symptom_Description: Entire VLAN 10 is down. PC1 and PC2 cannot ping the gateway.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip interface brief ... Gi0/0 admin down down
Expected_Fault: The physical router interface GigabitEthernet0/0 connecting to Switch S1 is shut down.

Symptom_Description: VLAN 20 devices (PC3/PC4) cannot ping the gateway. VLAN 10 works fine.
Show_Command_Output: Sw# show interfaces trunk ... (Output is empty). show run int g0/1 ... switchport mode access
Expected_Fault: The trunk link between Switch Sw and Router0 is incorrectly configured as an access port.

Symptom_Description: PC1 has no link light. Cannot ping anything.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show interfaces status ... Fa0/1 disconnected down
Expected_Fault: The physical Ethernet cable between PC1 and Switch S1 is unplugged or deleted.

Symptom_Description: PC2 has no link light. Cannot ping anything.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show interfaces status ... Fa0/2 admin down down
Expected_Fault: Switch port FastEthernet0/2 is administratively shut down.

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping the gateway or any other device.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show vlan brief ... 99 active Fa0/1
Expected_Fault: PC1's switch port (Fa0/1) is assigned to the wrong VLAN (VLAN 99 instead of VLAN 10).

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping the gateway. VLAN 10 routing fails.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show run interface g0/0.10 ... encapsulation dot1Q 99
Expected_Fault: The router subinterface is configured to encapsulate the wrong VLAN ID (99 instead of 10).

Symptom_Description: PC1 and PC2 lose all connectivity. Link lights might be on but no pings.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show vlan brief ... (VLAN 10 is completely missing from the list)
Expected_Fault: VLAN 10 was deleted from the switch's VLAN database.

Symptom_Description: PC3 cannot ping the gateway. VLAN 20 routing fails.
Show_Command_Output: Sw# show vlan brief ... 10 active Fa0/1
Expected_Fault: PC3's switch port (Fa0/1) is assigned to VLAN 10 instead of its correct VLAN 20.

Symptom_Description: PC3 and PC4 cannot ping outside VLAN 20. Gateway is unreachable.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip interface brief ... Gi0/0.20 admin down down
Expected_Fault: The router subinterface for VLAN 20 (Gi0/0.20) is administratively shut down.

Symptom_Description: Router sends traffic to a black hole. Specific subnets become unreachable.
Expected_Fault: A fake default static route is pointing to a non-existent next-hop IP address (192.168.10.99).

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping PC3 or PC4. Inter-VLAN routing fails for VLAN 20.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip route ... S 192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, Null0
Expected_Fault: A static route for VLAN 20 is pointing to the Null0 interface (a blackhole route).

Symptom_Description: VLAN 20 is completely down. Switch Sw cannot reach the router.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip interface brief ... Gi0/1 192.168.30.1 up up
Expected_Fault: The physical interface connecting to Switch Sw has the wrong IP address, breaking the link.

Symptom_Description: PC3 and PC4 cannot ping the gateway.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip interface brief ... Gi0/0.20 unassigned up up
Expected_Fault: The IP address was removed from the VLAN 20 subinterface.

Symptom_Description: PC1 can ping the gateway, but routing fails for some external destinations.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show run interface g0/0.10 ... ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.0.0
Expected_Fault: Router subinterface has an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.0.0 instead of 255.255.255.0).

Symptom_Description: PC1 is set to DHCP but gets a 169.254.x.x address. Cannot reach network.
Show_Command_Output: PC1> ipconfig ... IP: 169.254.x.x. Router0# show run | include dhcp ... (Missing network command)
Expected_Fault: The DHCP pool on the router is missing the network statement to define the IP range.

Symptom_Description: PC1 is set to DHCP but gets a 169.254.x.x address.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show ip dhcp pool ... (Shows 0 available addresses). show run | include excluded ... 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.254
Expected_Fault: The DHCP excluded-address range covers the entire subnet, leaving no IPs to lease.

Symptom_Description: PC1 gets an IP via DHCP but cannot ping PC3 (Inter-VLAN routing fails).
Show_Command_Output: PC1> ipconfig ... Gateway: 192.168.10.99. Router0# show run | include dhcp ... default-router 192.168.10.99
Expected_Fault: The DHCP server is assigning an incorrect default gateway to the clients.

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot resolve server names (e.g., ping server1 fails), but pinging IPs works.
Show_Command_Output: PC1> ipconfig ... DNS Server: 8.8.8.8. PC1> nslookup server1 ... DNS request timed out.
Expected_Fault: DNS server is set to an unreachable external IP (8.8.8.8) instead of the local DNS server.

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot resolve server names. Pinging the DNS server IP works.
Show_Command_Output: PC1> nslookup server1 ... Server: 192.168.10.50 ... Non-existent domain.
Expected_Fault: The local DNS server is running but has no host (A) records configured in its database.

Symptom_Description: PC1 cannot ping PC3. Request timed out. Other traffic might work.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show access-lists 100 ... deny icmp any any. show run int g0/0.10 ... ip access-group 100 in
Expected_Fault: An inbound ACL on the router gateway is explicitly blocking ICMP (ping) traffic.

Symptom_Description: PC3 cannot access the web server on PC1 (port 80). Pings work fine.
Show_Command_Output: Router0# show access-lists 101 ... deny tcp any any eq 80. show run int g0/0.20 ... ip access-group 101 in
Expected_Fault: An inbound ACL is blocking TCP port 80 (HTTP) traffic from reaching the server.

Symptom_Description: Wireless Laptop cannot connect to the wireless network at all.
Show_Command_Output: Laptop Desktop -> Wireless Tab ... SSID is set to Guest_Net (AP is broadcasting Corp_Net)
Expected_Fault: The wireless laptop is configured with the wrong SSID (Network Name).

Symptom_Description: Wireless Laptop shows Connected but gets a 169.254.x.x IP and cannot ping.
Show_Command_Output: Laptop Desktop -> Wireless Tab ... Password is incorrect. AP Security settings show WPA2 passphrase mismatch.
Expected_Fault: The Wi-Fi security passphrase (WPA2 password) typed on the laptop is incorrect.

Symptom_Description: Wireless clients connected to the AP cannot get an IP or ping the gateway.
Show_Command_Output: S1# show interfaces status ... Fa0/3 (Port where AP is connected) admin down down
Expected_Fault: The switch port connecting to the Wireless Access Point is administratively shut down.
